claim: Kahneman and Klein (2009) is a real American Psychologist paper titled 'Conditions for intuitive expertise: A failure to disagree'; Crossref confirms the record but its abstract could not be opened.
quote: Conditions for intuitive expertise: A failure to disagree.
title: Conditions for intuitive expertise: A failure to disagree
transfer: Known thesis (memory, not verified here): trust a fast first answer only when the environment is regular and the person had long practice with feedback. Agent step: classify the task as regular or irregular before choosing doubt or no doubt.

claim: CHECK: The claim 'first-answer intuition is reliable only in regular environments with feedback' could not be verified from the text. Only the bibliographic record was opened (PubMed, PsycNet and ResearchGate were blocked or empty). Verdict: unverified, keep as memory-level.
title: Conditions for intuitive expertise: A failure to disagree
transfer: none until the text is opened

claim: Teng and Lien (2022, PLOS ONE, 90 analyzed) found an incubation effect only for the mindfulness-induced group, only on flexibility; the mind-wandering-prone group showed none, and fluency and originality showed no main effect of condition.
quote: the mindfulness-induced group (N = 30) outperformed the control group (N = 31) on flexibility for the unusual uses task
title: Propensity or diversity? Investigating how mind wandering influences the incubation effect of creativity
transfer: A break helps little and only on flexibility. A context reset in an agent should be tested, not assumed to help.

claim: CHECK: Incubation rests on more than one source in existence terms (Sio and Ormerod 2009 plus later studies), but the later study opened here found a weak, conditional effect. No preregistered replication was found. Verdict: stays 'small and conditional'.
title: incubation check
transfer: Run the cheap context-reset test; expect little.

claim: Across three studies with six LLMs, LLM creativity ratings moderately track human ratings; LLMs use a narrower set of human standards, agree most on novelty, and barely change when context changes (preprint, v2 Sep 2026).
quote: LLMs generally relied on a narrower subset of human creativity evaluation standards.
authors: Lyu, P.; Kim, Y.J.; Xiao, H.; Luan, Y.L.
title: Why Large Language Models and Humans Converge and Diverge in Evaluating Creativity
transfer: An LLM judge can screen novelty but should not decide feasibility or fit; add task-specific checks outside the judge.

claim: In a marketing creativity benchmark with 11,012 pairwise human comparisons, models clustered tightly (top beats bottom about 61% of the time) and three LLM-as-judge setups correlated weakly and inconsistently with human rankings.
quote: weak, inconsistent correlations and judge-specific biases
authors: Bhat, N.; Browne, K.; Bingemann, P.
title: Creativity Benchmark: A benchmark for marketing creativity for large language models
transfer: Do not let one LLM judge pick the best idea alone. Keep several candidates or add a human or executable check.

claim: Si, Yang and Hashimoto's blind comparison of over 100 NLP researchers against an LLM ideation agent found LLM ideas rated more novel but slightly less feasible, and names LLM self-evaluation failure and low idea diversity as open problems.
authors: Si, C.; Yang, D.; Hashimoto, T.
title: Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas?
transfer: Generation can be novel; selection by the same model is the weak link. Use a separate feasibility check.

claim: CHECK: 'LLM judges can pick the best creative idea from many candidates' is not supported by what was opened. Two preprints report weak or moderate agreement with humans and one reports a self-evaluation failure. Verdict: selection by an LLM judge is weak evidence, especially for feasibility.
authors: Bhat et al. 2025; Lyu et al. 2026; Si et al. 2024
title: LLM-as-judge creativity check
transfer: Treat the judge as a filter for obvious weak ideas only.
